The workspace-state capture now reads a workspace's whole supervisord config: the main `system/supervisord.conf`, plus every drop-in under `system/supervisord.conf.d/`.

That capture is what tells a delivered app from an unsupervised one. It joins each registry row to the program that registered it by scanning the config's `[program:*]` blocks for their `forward_port.py` calls, and it was catting the main config alone. A workspace template is free to declare each program in its own `supervisord.conf.d/<name>.conf` drop-in, and the default template now does; against such a workspace the capture found no `[program:*]` section at all, so the join came back empty.

Two things went wrong from there, both silently, since an app-free workspace produces the same empty result. A multi-port app's extra origin rows (`<name>-admin`) own no program of their own, so with no config join they were recorded as having nothing supervising them. More costly: the pre-existing-registration resolution has no fallback, so a template app whose service had not registered its port by the time the snapshot was taken appeared in neither half of the pre-existing set and was scored as something the agent had delivered.

The capture now also says when it could not read the config whole, instead of answering as though the workspace supervised nothing. supervisord takes its programs from the config the capture reads, so a `supervisorctl status` listing that names programs while the capture declares none is a read that missed part of the config -- which is what any template layout the capture does not follow looks like from outside. The pre-existing set then reports unknown rather than a set that silently omits a template app, and a row whose owning program could not be resolved is recorded as an error against the harness rather than as an app the agent left unsupervised. The check keys on declared `[program:*]`/`[eventlistener:*]` sections rather than on `forward_port.py` calls, so a template whose apps all register their ports at runtime is not mistaken for a broken read.

The drop-in directory is assumed, not parsed out of the config's `[include]` glob: `system/supervisord.conf.d/` is the default template's convention, and the template's own layout test pins its include glob to that directory. The capture is a `cat` of the main file followed by a shell glob over the quoted path, so a workspace path containing a space stays one path, and a workspace with no drop-in directory (every already-released template) reads exactly as before.

Because the capture is now several files concatenated, two things about block boundaries had to be right. Full-line comments are dropped before the blocks are scanned: a drop-in's leading prose routinely describes the `forward_port.py` call its program makes, and it would otherwise have been read as a registration by the last program of the file before it. And a block now ends at the next section of any kind rather than the next `[program:*]`, so the `[eventlistener:*]` the template ships mid-order is no longer scanned as part of the program before it.
